papers.title: An investigation of novel population models to control aphid outbreaks via a data driven “adaptive” framework
papers.authors: Aniket Banerjee, Urvashi Verma, Satyam Narayan Srivastava, Rana D. Parshad
papers.abstract: The soybean aphid ( Aphis glycines ) is an invasive pest that causes severe yield loss to soybeans in the North Central United States. Its populations frequently exhibit multiple, unequal-amplitude peaks within a single growing season, a pattern that classical boom-bust models cannot reproduce. We investigate and develop a sequence of population models aimed at capturing this multi-peak behaviour while remaining biologically realistic and useful for pest management. We first show that the variable carrying capacity model (VCM), in which seasonally fluctuating host-plant quality drives a time-dependent carrying capacity, can generate multiple peaks but also admits finite-time blow-up, or population explosion, rendering it unrealistic for high colonisations. We propose an adaptive behavioural model with a density-dependent switch that preserves the multi-peak dynamics while guaranteeing bounded populations. papers.title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
papers.authors: A. Suresh kumar, C. Rajan
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Smart Infrastructure and Environmental Sustainability
papers.abstract: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. papers.title: The ecological adaptability of pinewood nematode populations: survival strategies, mechanisms and co‐evolution
papers.authors: Chen‐Xi Ying, Tong‐Yue Wen, Xiao‐Lei Ding, Xiao‐Qin Wu
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (pinewood nematode, PWN) is the causal agent of pine wilt disease and ranks among the most destructive invasive pests threatening global forest ecosystems. Since its introduction to China, this nematode has triggered massive ecological and economic losses, while its distribution range continues to expand northward. The association between the widespread dispersal of B. xylophilus in invaded areas and the ecological adaptability of its populations has drawn considerable attention. RESULTS: This review systematically synthesizes recent research advances regarding the ecological adaptability of PWN populations, elaborating on molecular mechanisms and ecological strategies that enable the nematode to colonize novel environments. In terms of thermal adaptation, differentially expressed genes, small heat shock protein families and the accumulation of key metabolites collectively shape adaptive pathways to resist extreme high and low temperature stress. For host adaptation, PWN displays polyphagous feeding habits and relies on diverse arboreal fungi as nutritional resources when pines were weakened or died. papers.title: Using Multispectral Imaging and Artificial Intelligence to Detect Crop Diseases and Pests Early
papers.authors: Idowu Olugbenga Adewumi, Babajide Saheed Kosemani
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Plant Diseases and Protection
papers.abstract: Abstract In sustainable agriculture, detecting pests and diseases early is critical. Recent technological advances in deep learning (DL) and multimodal imaging like multispectral and thermal data crop health monitoring is promising. Despite the progress, obtaining high accuracy across various crops with real-time performance is still a challenge. The hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)-attention model integrating multispectral and thermal data for pest and disease detection has been introduced. A total of 1760 samples were collected from six crops (maize, rice, wheat, tomato and cassava), across different growth stages, labelled fungal, bacterial, viral and pest infections. The data was divided into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test sets. 3,500 samples were used for training. 750 samples were used for validation and test set. The hybrid CNN-attention model was contrasted with certain baseline models (SVM, Random Forest, CNN-RGB, CNN-Multispectral) and certain fusion methods (early, late, and hybrid fusion) based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and early detection sensitivity. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: Context Balancing food security and biodiversity conservation is a major challenge in the Galapagos Islands, where agriculture overlaps with vulnerable native ecosystems. Objective We evaluated the potential of local agricultural production in Santa Cruz, Galapagos, to increase food self-sufficiency while conserving native vegetation under future population growth, and assessed the effects of land use change on invasive plant cover. Methods We developed the Galapagos Land Use (GAL-LU) model, a farm-level multi-objective optimization model integrating agricultural production, nutrient self-sufficiency, farm income, land-use allocation, and invasive plant dynamics. The model combined biophysical, economic, nutritional, and land-cover data for 182 farms in Santa Cruz. Scenarios were evaluated under projected population growth from 2022 to 2100 and different nutritional targets. papers.title: Integrated computational pipelines using machine learning and deep neural networks for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease classification
papers.authors: Veeresh Kondapaneni, Yash Melkani, Girish Chandra Melkani
papers.abstract: Abstract High-speed optical microscopy of Drosophila hearts has become an essential approach for modeling cardiovascular disease and aging. However, manual evaluation of cardiac function is time-consuming, subjective, and error-prone, highlighting the need for reliable computational frameworks. Here, we present an end-to-end dual-modality pipeline that combines segmentation-derived cardiac parameters with ensemble machine learning and raw video-based representations with deep convolutional neural networks. This integrated approach enables automated and quantitative phenotyping of cardiac function across both aging and cardiovascular disease contexts. We evaluated the performance of the pipeline across three biological problems relevant to cardiovascular systems biology: distinguishing between young (1-week) and aged (5-week) hearts, classifying healthy hearts from those carrying the lamin C mutation (LamC G489V ), and identifying phenotypes associated with Ogdh knockdown. papers.authors: Pengcheng Ma, Zhifeng Guo, Zhirui Guo, Yue Pang, Zhidong Zhang
papers.abstract: Thinning can improve stand spatial structure but removes living biomass carbon, creating a trade-off that may vary among stand types and future climate pathways. We developed a spatially explicit, climate-sensitive multi-objective computational framework that integrates an individual-tree growth model, five neighborhood-based spatial metrics, species-specific biomass equations, and Monte Carlo optimization. The framework was applied to 15 mapped plots comprising secondary Betula platyphylla forests, Larix principis-rupprechtii–B. platyphylla mixed forests, and L. principis-rupprechtii plantations in northern China. Stand development was projected from 2025 to 2030 under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, and thinning was optimized under carbon-retention, balanced, and structure-priority objectives. Across stand types, the best-found thinning intensity increased from 5.0–12.0% under the carbon-retention objective to 32.1–41.0% under the balanced objective and 44.2–49.3% under the structure-priority objective. papers.title: When more information is not enough: AI-enabled advisory and coordinated farming decisions under uncertainty among smallholder farmers in the Mekong Delta
papers.authors: Dinh Duc Truong, Nguyen Dieu Hang, Duong Duc Tam, Duong Thi Van Anh
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of digitally mediated and increasingly AI-enabled agricultural advisory systems, more information does not necessarily lead to more coordinated farming decisions under uncertainty. This study reconceptualizes AI-enabled advisory as a coordination-support mechanism and examines how it is associated with coordinated decision-making through three behavioural capacities: understanding system interactions, operational coordination capability, and adaptive complexity management. Using a survey dataset of 386 smallholder rice farmers from An Giang, Tra Vinh, and Ca Mau provinces in Vietnam's Mekong Delta, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that AI-enabled advisory is positively associated with all three behavioural capacities, while adaptive complexity management has the strongest association with coordinated decision-making capability (β = 0.33, p < 0.001). It also represents the strongest indirect pathway between AI-enabled advisory and coordinated decision-making (β = 0.135, p < 0.001). papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). papers.authors: Yanru Huang, Chaoyang Wu, Wenjiang Huang, Yang Liu, Man Qi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Climate change is altering life-cycle timing and may disrupt coordinated interactions between flowering plants and flower-visiting insects. Using Global Biodiversity Information Facility observation records from Europe between 2000 and 2024, we compiled a continental-scale phenological dataset covering flowering periods of 707 angiosperm species and adult activity periods of 620 Lepidoptera species. We extracted the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles and activity-window width and used linear mixed-effects models to analyse spatio-temporal trends. The results showed that plant phenology advanced significantly, with the 10th and 50th percentiles shifting earlier by -0.597 and -0.507 d yr⁻¹, respectively, whereas the 90th percentile showed no significant change; flowering-window width increased by 0.361 d yr⁻¹. By contrast, Lepidoptera phenology advanced evenly across the season, with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles shifting by -0.137, -0.153 and -0.155 d yr⁻¹, respectively, while activity-window width showed no significant change. papers.title: From data-driven differential equations to mechanistic forecasting with machine learning
papers.authors: Amit K. Chakraborty, Hao Wang, Pouria Ramazi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of The Royal Society Interface
papers.abstract: The equations of complex dynamical systems may not be identified by expert knowledge, especially if the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Data-driven discovery methods address this challenge by inferring governing equations from time-series data using a library of functions constructed from the measured variables. However, these methods typically assume time-invariant coefficients, which limits their ability to capture evolving system dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we allow some of the parameters to vary over time, learn their temporal evolution directly from data and infer a system of equations that incorporates both constant and time-varying parameters. We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. The model is validated on simulated susceptible-infected-recovered and consumer-resource systems, as well as on real-world greenhouse gas concentration and cyanobacteria cell count datasets. papers.authors: Ali Zia, Ali Zia, Usman Ali, Charissa Yu, Jun Wei Zhou
papers.abstract: Spectral 3D computer vision combines wavelength-resolved measurements with geometric information to support material-aware reconstruction, perception, and scene analysis. However, the literature remains fragmented across hyperspectral and multispectral sensing, cross-spectral depth and pose estimation, spectral point clouds, LiDAR–hyperspectral fusion, and neural scene representations. This survey provides a structured review of the field, covering spectral and geometric acquisition, data representations, calibration and registration, spectral 3D reconstruction, integrated spectral 3D acquisition and joint physical modelling, learning-based methods, downstream tasks, benchmark datasets, applications, and software tools. We organise existing methods into three complementary methodological themes: spectral support for 3D information estimation, spectral 3D reconstruction and mapping, and integrated spectral 3D acquisition and joint physical modelling. papers.title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
papers.authors: Xingyi Guo, Linshuoshuo Lyu, Chao Li, Chao Li, Ghadeer K. Dawwas
papers.abstract: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conducted genome-wide association meta-analyses of 63,415 IBD cases of European and East Asian descendants and identified 90 previously unknown risk loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing (AS-WAS), and alternative polyadenylation (APA-WAS) analyses using RNA-seq data from normal colon tissues of 707 European and 364 East Asian individuals, we uncovered 506 high-confidence IBD risk genes, including 384 not previously reported. These genes converge on immune regulation, microbial interaction, and other pathways central to IBD pathogenesis, with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. Notably, 46 risk genes are targeted by 225 drugs that have been approved or in Phase II/III trials, including sulfasalazine already used in IBD therapy. Our study findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and support the development of precision medicine for its prevention and treatment.

papers.abstract: Lately, sustainability has dominated academic, practice and policy discourse. The construction industry is singled out as one of the unsustainable sectors due to its linear methods of extract-use-dispose. Globally, linear construction practices are responsible for approximately 50% of raw material extraction, 36% of all emissions, 40% of energy consumption and 50% of waste resulting in natural resource scarcity and waste management catastrophes. In Africa, only 4% of the waste is recycled, whereas 90% is illegally dumped, and the balance is unaccounted for. Consequently, circular economy (circularity), anchored on reduce, reuse, and recycle principles, is widely perceived as a sustainable alternative to linearity. The primary objective of circularity in the construction industry is to advance sustainability by creating a circular built environment. Closely related to circularity, sustainable construction practices also pursue sustainability. papers.title: DNA barcoding of more than one million insect specimens indicates that at least one third of California's insect biodiversity remains undiscovered
papers.authors: Austin J. Baker, Brad Balukjian, Hilary Bayer, Jen Bayer, Daniel Gluesenkamp
papers.abstract: Insects are the most diverse terrestrial organisms, yet they are underrepresented in large-scale conservation assessments. To address this gap, the California Insect Barcoding Initiative is developing a publicly accessible, statewide DNA-barcode reference library for California insects to support scalable surveys, establish baseline biodiversity measurements, and generate potential distribution maps that inform conservation planning. Specimens are collected with a hybrid strategy that combines standardized Malaise trapping, to enable replicable sampling, and opportunistic collecting, to maximize taxonomic coverage. To date, we have barcoded over one million specimens; preliminary completeness analyses suggest that current sampling captures roughly 65–69% of the fauna, implying a conservative minimum of circa 61,000 insect species in California. Using all sequenced specimen records, we generated rule-based spatial range interpolations constrained by ecoregion and vegetation type, and used these to infer spatial patterns in insect species richness across the state. papers.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic responses of Botrytis cinerea under L-carvone fumigation
papers.authors: Zhaoyu Ren, Qisen Lu, Chunling Yang, Weichen You, Chen Wang
papers.abstract: Abstract Botrytis cinerea , a necrotrophic phytopathogenic fungus with a wide host range, causes severe postharvest gray mold and huge economic losses worldwide. Conventional chemical fungicides easily induce multidrug resistance in field isolates, while the natural monoterpene volatile L-carvone exhibits broad-spectrum antifungal activity. However, the comprehensive molecular mechanism by which L-carvone suppresses B. cinerea remains unclear. In this study, mycelia of B. cinerea were treated with L-carvone at EC 50 concentration with sterile water as blank control. RNA-seq transcriptome and HS-SPME-GC-MS untargeted metabolome sequencing were performed to systematically dissect molecular responses via integrated omics analysis. A total of 1,531 DEGs were identified, including 347 upregulated and 1,184 downregulated genes. Upregulated DEGs were enriched in sulfur metabolism, cysteine and methionine metabolism involved in transient antioxidant response, whereas downregulated DEGs mainly participated in cell membrane lipid biosynthesis, carbon energy metabolism, phytotoxin synthesis and conidiation. papers.title: Temporal dynamics drive soil resistome variation more strongly than warming or biocide application
papers.authors: Fernando Ruiz-Torrubia, Carlos Garbisu, Mikel Anza, Val F. Lanza, Teresa M. Coque
papers.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic resistance is a major global health concern. Understanding how climate change-related factors can influence antimicrobial resistance patterns in the environment is essential for developing efficient One Health-based resistance control strategies. In this study, under field conditions, we assessed the combined effects of soil warming and biocide (herbicide, fungicide, insecticide) application on soil physicochemical and microbial parameters, potato yield, and the soil resistome using the targeted metagenomics ResCap platform to quantify antimicrobial resistance genes (i.e., antibiotic resistance genes, metal resistance genes, biocide resistance genes, relaxase genes).
